title: Finite-rank error after adjusting a coefficient section
statement: Let $k\subseteq K$ be fields of characteristic $p>0$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative local $k$-algebra, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $r:\Lambda\to K$ be a ring map compatible with the $k$-structures and with kernel $\mathfrak m$. Fix a finite subset $t\subset\Lambda$ spanning $\mathfrak m$ as an ideal. Let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be an ideal with $\mathfrak mI=0$. Let $\sigma_0:K\to\Lambda$ be a section of $r$ and $c_0\subset K$ a finite subset. Let $\psi:k\to\Lambda$ be a ring map equal to the structure map $i$ modulo $I$, whose values lie in $\operatorname{Subring.closure}(t\cup\sigma_0(k(c_0)))$. Assume $H_1(L_{K/k})$ is finite dimensional over $K$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Then there exist a section $\sigma:K\to\Lambda$ of $r$, unchanged from $\sigma_0$ modulo $I$, and a finite subset $f\subset I$, such that for each $a\in k$ there is $b\in\operatorname{Subring.closure}(t\cup\sigma(k(c_0)))$ with $i(a)-b\in\operatorname{span}_k(f)$. Here derivations and their universal modules are as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and span uses the given $k$-algebra action on $\Lambda$.

source.place: Tag 07FG, proof of the coefficient-field claim (read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07FG)

proof.text: The condition mI=0 equips I with its canonical K-vector-space action through r. The difference theta=i-psi lands in I, and expanding the product identity shows it is a derivation over the prime field. Choose a differential basis dy_j of Omega_k over the prime field, using that differentials span and that a spanning family contains a basis.

The Jacobi--Zariski sequence at K tensor Omega_k identifies the kernel of the differential map with the image of H1(K/k). It is finite dimensional, so a finite subset J0 of the extended differential basis supports the kernel. Linear independence of the full basis implies independence of the images dy_j outside J0.

Extend these independent images to a K-basis of Omega_K. Define a K-linear map to I agreeing with theta on the chosen basis vectors outside J0 and zero on additional vectors. Compose with the universal derivation to obtain D:K to I. Then theta-D restricted to k is supported on J0, and its values are in the k-span of the finite set f_j given by its values at dy_j for j in J0.

Set sigma=sigma0+D. Because I squared is zero and mI=0, direct expansion proves it is a ring map and a section, with the same reduction modulo I. For an expression representing psi(a) in the generated subring, replace sigma0 coefficients by sigma coefficients. Products involving a positive-degree t term have zero correction because t lies in m. The constant correction equals D(r(psi(a)))=D(algebraMap k K a). This identity is independent of the expression; it can be proved by induction on subring closure, using the product rule for D. The new expression b lies in the same finite coefficient closure for sigma. Its difference from i(a) is theta(a)-D(a), which belongs to span_k(f_j).
